newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Guards arrested after fatal Venezuala prison fire.
newsitem.headline: Guards arrested after fatal Venezuala prison fire.

text.p: Three guards at a crowded Venezuelan jail were ordered arrested after 1,800 inmates went on a hunger strike to demand justice after a fire killed 25 prisoners last week, prison officials said on Thursday.

The inmates at La Planta jail in southwest Caracas began the fast on Wednesday afternoon. The protest was peaceful, one official told Reuters by telephone, but inmates "want those responsible for the fire brought to justice and punished."
A judge ordered the detention of three national guardsmen who Justice Ministry officials said started the fire on Oct. 22.

Judge Maximiliano Fuenmayor, who also ordered the arrest of a Justice Ministry employee, told reporters the investigation showed that the three lobbed tear gas canisters into a small cell with about 40 inmates locked inside.
The guards had already been placed at the disposition of an investigating military judge. The National Guard provides additional security at Venezuela's overcrowded and violent jails.

Converted from an army barracks more than 30 years ago, La Planta jail is supposed to hold 300 prisoners. Jammed and decaying, it is typical of Venezuela's 32 jails, widely considered among the most dangerous in Latin America.
